extracted.intended_audience: researchers and inventors affiliated with Stanford University, Stanford Health Care, or Lucile Packard Children's Hospital
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for when and how Stanford-affiliated researchers should confidentially disclose inventions to the Office of Technology Licensing (OTL) to preserve potential patent rights and initiate licensing/technology transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to submit — commercial potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever you have research results that may have a commercial potential, it is recommended that you submit a confidential Invention Disclosure Form to the OTL or contact us for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit when research results may have commercial potential; contact OTL at 650-723-0651 or otl@stanford.edu for consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential submission recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors are strongly encouraged to confidentially disclose their invention to OTL as early as possible in the inventive process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential disclosure helps OTL evaluate and protect IP; use the confidential Invention Disclosure Form or contact OTL for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit before any public disclosure to preserve patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to preserve potential patent rights, we strongly encourage inventors to confidentially disclose their invention to OTL as early as possible in the inventive process and before a public disclosure of your inventions or results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosures can jeopardize patent rights; see list of what counts as public disclosure and contact OTL immediately if public disclosure is imminent.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes public disclosure (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public disclosures include, but are not limited to, journal and website publications, presentations at conferences or seminars (including open seminars at Stanford), posters, dissertations or master theses, pre-prints, and abstract publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these activities as potentially destroying novelty for patenting; avoid them prior to confidential disclosure or discuss mitigation with OTL.

rubrics_metrics.name: If planning imminent public disclosure, contact Licensing Manager immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to have any public disclosure in the near future, please directly reach out to the Licensing Manager that you work with and discuss the next viable steps as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not know who to contact, reach out to otl@stanford.edu right away and OTL will connect you with the appropriate Licensing Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the OTL online researcher portal for formal disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use OTL’s online researcher portal to submit a confidential formal disclosure of your invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided on the page (Submit an Invention); the portal is the official route for filing the Invention Disclosure Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — affiliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This website is only for submission of ideas and inventions created by people while affiliated with Stanford University, Stanford Health Care or Lucile Packard Children's Hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only inventions created during affiliation with these institutions should be submitted via this portal; external inventors should contact appropriate channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional resources — Inventor FAQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Need more clarification about the invention disclosure process? See our Inventor FAQ: Submit an Invention section to read more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAQ provides further details about the process; consult it for common questions and procedural clarifications.
